instruction: Using Visual Studio Code, create a Python script named `worldbank_canada_gdp_inflation_analysis.py` inside `/home/user/analysis_results/worldbank_data/`. First, open Google Chrome and navigate to `https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/889392-about-the-indicators-api-documentation`. Review the correct API request format. Then, construct two API endpoints using the official World Bank API structure: (1) `https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/CA/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD?format=json&per_page=500` for Canada GDP, and (2) `https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/CA/indicator/FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG?format=json&per_page=500` for Canada Inflation. Use `requests` to retrieve data from both endpoints, handle pagination if present, and extract the last five available years and their values. Create one DataFrame with columns: `year`, `gdp`, and `inflation`. Compute the correlation between GDP and inflation, and determine the year with the maximum divergence defined as `|GDP_t − mean(GDP)| + |Inflation_t − mean(Inflation)|`. Save the result to a text file named `canada_gdp_inflation_summary.txt` formatted exactly as: `Correlation: <value>, Max_Divergence_Year: <year>`.
